does: Mixes flour, warm water, yeast and salt into a very wet, sticky dough and beats it by hand in a bowl, with a wet hand, lifting and slapping it, until it turns stretchy and full of air. It is far too soft to knead on a board.

intro.what: Sfenj uses a very wet dough beaten by hand in a bowl until stretchy and bubbly.
intro.why: The stickiness is part of the method. Learning to work with it preserves the airy texture instead of turning it into a firm kneading dough.

how: Stir the yeast into part of the warm water with the sugar and let it foam.
Put the flour and the salt in a large bowl and pour in the yeast water and the rest of the water.
Beat with a wet hand, lifting the dough high and letting it fall back, again and again.
Keep beating until the dough is smooth, elastic and bubbly, and drops from the hand in a slow rope.

cues.text: The dough is sticky and soft, and stretches in a long strand without breaking.
Bubbles show on the surface and the dough no longer sticks in lumps to the bowl.

mistakes.mistake: Adding more flour to stop the stickiness, which makes a dense doughnut.
mistakes.fix: Keep the dough wet and wet the hand instead.

mistakes.mistake: Stopping too soon, which leaves a dough without air.
mistakes.fix: Beat until it stretches and bubbles.

quiz.question: Why keep sfenj dough wet rather than firm?
choices: A firmer dough develops the same texture without beating.
Extra flour creates the air bubbles instead of beating.
The wet dough supports the intended airy texture.
quiz.because: Adding flour to remove stickiness changes this soft dough toward a denser result.

quiz.question: How is this dough worked?
choices: Lift and slap it in the bowl with a wet hand.
Knead it on a board with extra flour.
Press it flat and leave it unworked.
quiz.because: The dough is too soft for board kneading; bowl beating develops stretch and incorporates air.

quiz.question: What shows that beating has developed the dough?
choices: It remains short and tears before stretching.
It stretches in strands and shows bubbles.
It stays in sticky lumps without visible bubbles.
quiz.because: Stretch and visible bubbles are the texture and air clues used in this method.

quiz.question: The dough feels too sticky to handle. What should you change?
choices: Add flour until it becomes a firm ball.
Dust the bowl heavily and stop beating.
Wet your hand rather than adding flour.
quiz.because: Wetting the hand makes the sticky dough easier to work while preserving its intended softness.

variant_of.differs: Kneading works a firm dough on a board with the heels of the hands. This dough is too wet for that: it is beaten in a bowl with a wet hand until it stretches, and it is never shaped until it goes into the oil.
